messages:
kai: Heads-up — noticed the cluster-autoscaler spawned 6 GPU nodes in us-west-2 over the last hour. App latency spiked; some model-serving pods ended up Pending then bounced. :grimacing:
morgan: Oof. Do we have taints on GPU pools now? last change to nodepool labels/taints?
leah: We tainted the gpu pool last quarter with key=redwood.com/gpu,value=true:NoSchedule to keep regular workloads off. most model-serving pods were updated to tolerate it but i think a recent helm bump removed the toleration.
sam: Can you paste the taints output?
kai: sure — ran on a node we scaled up:
```
$ kubectl describe node ip-10-0-3-12.us-west-2.compute.internal | grep -A2 Taints
Taints: redwood.com/gpu=true:NoSchedule
```
morgan: yep that's the one. pods missing the toleration will stay Pending and trigger CA to add nodes, then other schedulable pods get evicted. bad feedback loop.
leah: The offending chart change was here — pod spec had tolerations removed in values.yml. i can revert but we should harden.
jessica: Suggestion: add nodeAffinity + toleration to the model-serving deployment so it strongly prefers GPU nodes and tolerates the taint. Example toleration snippet i use:
```yaml
tolerations:
  - key: "redwood.com/gpu"
    operator: "Equal"
    value: "true"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
nodeAffinity:
  requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
    nodeSelectorTerms:
      - matchExpressions:
          - key: "kubernetes.io/instance-type"
            operator: In
            values: ["p4d", "a100"]
```
sam: Also consider PreferNoSchedule on non-critical gpu nodes for burst capacity? or use taint with NoExecute for strict isolation. depends on how we want eviction behavior.
morgan: For autoscaler behavior: CA sees pending pods unschedulable and will add nodes. If pods never tolerate the taint we keep scaling. We should gate scale-up by ensuring scheduler predicates succeed — tolerations fix that. Also set cluster-autoscaler expander to prioritize older pools.
kai: i don't want to rely on manual chart changes everywhere. can we add a mutating webhook that injects the toleration for pods labeled workload=redwood-model?
leah: we discussed that in infra-op morning — feasible. webhook + admission rule: if pod has label redwood.ai/needs-gpu: "true" then add toleration + nodeAffinity. fallback: add namespace-level default tolerations via LimitRange? (no, not for tolerations).
jessica: quick patch we can do now: add toleration back to the chart's deployment template and rollout a canary of 10% replicas. monitor autoscaler and node counts for 30m.
infra-bot: deploy triggered: model-serving v2.14.1 -> canary (10%): rollout started by jessica at 2025-11-22T14:47:02Z
morgan: after the canary, watch these commands: `kubectl get pods -n models -o wide` and `kubectl get nodes -o custom-columns=NAME:metadata.name,TAINTS:spec.taints`
kai: action items: 1) leah revert chart change + add unit test to chart CI to check toleration presence (leah) 2) infra: evaluate mutating webhook for label-based injection (sam) 3) ops: monitor autoscale behavior and cost delta for next 24h (morgan) 4) jessica keep canary and report after 30m (jessica)
leah: got it. i'll open a PR and add a helm test that ensures `tolerations` exists when `needsGpu=true`.
sam: i'll draft the webhook proposal — will include logic for nodeAffinity too so we avoid accidental scheduling on wrong instance types.
morgan: FYI the scale-up cost for the burst was ~ $1.8k in cloud spend this morning per cost dashboard. we should add an alert if CA adds >3 gpu nodes in 1h. :money_with_wings:
kai: agreed. set alert and also add a CA throttle policy — maybe increase `scale-down-delay` and `max-node-provision-time` to reduce churn.
jessica: can confirm canary pods landed on GPU nodes correctly and tolerated taint. no more pending. monitoring now. :thumbsup:
kai: thanks team. let's sync in ops-standup tomorrow if anything odd.
